explanation: `var i` is function-scoped, not block-scoped, so all three closures created inside the loop share the exact same variable binding. The loop finishes (setting `i` to 3) before any `setTimeout` callback actually runs, so every callback reads the same final value. The output is `3` three times, not `0, 1, 2` as the loop body might suggest. Swapping `var` for `let` would give each iteration its own binding and fix it.
